alternatives.full_local_argument: The rational-equivalence subgroup is generated by principal divisor cycles on integral subvarieties, using finite sums in the finite-type case and locally finite supporting families otherwise. On an affine chart of an integral supporting subvariety, write a rational function $a/b$ with $a,b$ nonzero. Its nonzero order can occur only at height-one primes containing $ab$. Such primes are minimal over $(ab)$, by the principal-ideal theorem in the domain, and there are finitely many because the ring is Noetherian. A finite affine cover gives global finiteness on a finite-type subvariety; otherwise it gives local finiteness. The local order function is already proved. On a normal subvariety its height-one local rings are DVRs, and the length order is exactly the ordinary Weil order. The quotient is therefore the stated Chow group. Top-dimensional cycles on an integral dimension-$n$ scheme give $A_n(X)=\mathbb Z[X]$, since no dimension-$(n+1)$ subvariety exists; cycles in greater dimensions vanish. Reduce the norm formula to a finite extension of one-dimensional local domains $A\subset B$ with fraction fields $K\subset L$.
For two full $A$-lattices $M,M'$ in a finite-dimensional $K$-space, their intersection has finite-colength in each. Define
$$\delta(M,M')=\ell_A(M/(M\cap M'))-\ell_A(M'/(M\cap M')).$$
A common lattice contained in three given lattices proves $\delta(M,M'')=\delta(M,M')+\delta(M',M'')$ by length additivity. Applying a $K$-linear automorphism to both lattices preserves lengths. An elementary transvection preserves a lattice obtained by scaling one standard basis vector to clear its denominator, so its index is zero. Gaussian elimination expresses every invertible matrix as elementary transvections and a diagonal matrix (row swaps are products of these and a diagonal unit), proving

For multiplication by $r\in L^*$ on the $A$-lattice $B$, its determinant is $N_{L/K}(r)$. Clear a denominator to reduce to $r\in B$; then the index is $\ell_A(B/rB)$. Decomposing this finite-length module over the maximal ideals $q$ of the semilocal $B$ gives
$$\operatorname{ord}_A(N_{L/K}r)=\sum_q[\kappa(q):\kappa(A)]\operatorname{ord}_{B_q}(r).$$
